mainEntity.name: What is different about Persian SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Half-spaces, digit forms, and the different spellings of the same word all change what search finds. We write with one consistent spelling, based on the phrase your audience actually types.

mainEntity.name: Do you produce content with AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every published text is written, or rewritten and checked, by one of us, and that person answers for it. AI tools can help with a draft. They never publish anything unchecked, and we don't produce filler articles. That is slower than mass production, and it is the only way we work.

mainEntity.name: Can the monthly agreement be stopped?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and the terms are in the written proposal: 30 days written notice before the end of the month. That's the whole mechanism, no surprises buried elsewhere.

Marketing and content
The likes roll in. The orders don't. Content that only looks good isn't doing its job, so we build yours around the questions customers ask before they buy, and around how they search.
Liked by everyone, bought by no one

Most businesses who come to us don't have a bad product. They have an audience that can't find them in search, and content that gets published without anyone knowing which piece answered a real question and which one just filled the calendar.

It happens when content is made away from the product: posts about everything except what the customer needs to know before buying. With no map of which question each piece answers, every month starts again from zero.

We're Roxana Negaresh and Arshia Amani, and we start with a search-intent map: your customers' real questions, and which piece of content answers each one, on which page. The monthly plan, the production and the technical SEO all sit on that one map. We don't promise Google rankings either; nobody can promise that honestly. What we hand over is content that belongs to your product, in a structure search can read. See the pattern in Instagram page or website: why a page is necessary for reach but not enough for a shop.
This works if

items: You have a clear product, and people still can't find you in search.
You need Persian content written properly: half-spaces, digits, and the words people actually search.
You need video or short writing that explains your product, not generic advertising noise.

blocks.html: Save your money if

items: You want a Google ranking promised to you. Nobody can honestly promise one.
You want bought followers, fake engagement, or articles mass-produced to fill pages.
Your product itself isn't clear yet. Then start with Business model design or UI/UX design, and come back.

blocks.html: Month by month

items: Structure. Input: your product, its customers and their real questions. Output: a search intent map, which question is answered by which content, on which page. Owner: dadmor with you.
Plan. Input: the intent map. Output: the month's content plan, channels included. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.

Produce. Input: the plan you approved, and access to the product or the people behind it. Output: the pieces themselves, text and video, each one approved by you before it goes out. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
Technical SEO. Input: your site. Output: a list of technical fixes: page titles and descriptions, structured data, speed, and half-spaces and digits in Persian content. Owner: dadmor.
Report. Input: what went out, and your analytics. Output: a monthly report of what was published and what we could measure. Owner: dadmor.

blocks.html: Deliverables
What changes the month

items: What sets the monthly band: pieces per month, the kind of piece (video is the heaviest work), channels, languages, and how much technical SEO is needed.
From you: access to the product and the people who know it, fast approval of drafts, and analytics access if you have it.
What slows a month down: approvals arriving late, and the product message changing mid-month.

blocks.html: The monthly band

items: A monthly S, M or L band, set by pieces, channels and SEO work. The fixed monthly price comes after the scoping conversation, in a written proposal.

blocks.html: The band is a starting estimate, and it moves with your real content calendar. The fixed monthly price is settled after we talk, in writing.
What we won't claim

items: We don't promise Google rankings. We deliver content that fits your product, the right structure and technical readiness. Where you land in search also depends on things outside our control.
No analytics? Then the monthly report can only say what was published, not what it achieved. We recommend privacy-friendly analytics.
Nothing goes out without your approval. We don't publish first and tell you later.
